scores.evidence: Critical path: "S1 → metadata → planner → executor → CLI → real-folder demo."
scores.rationale: Spikes and fixtures precede components, and the components build from pure substrate (metadata, scanner, planner, journal) up to executor, CLI and demo.

scores.evidence: M1: "Thin slice + spikes... preview/apply/undo for JPEG/HEIC... CI on 3 OSes; installable wheel" and a demo on a real folder copy.
scores.rationale: M1 is a real end-to-end slice that is installable and demonstrated before RAW, format and fallback features.

scores.evidence: D4 "Revisit if: Overwrite reports from users... → add RENAME_NOREPLACE"; D5 marked Hard with a revisit trigger.
scores.rationale: Decision table lists options, default, reversibility and flip conditions, with assumptions tagged and validated.

scores.evidence: "D5... The group is the unit of planning and journalling, so retrofitting it later would be costly." Spikes S1/S2 first, then planner/executor.
scores.rationale: Widest-impact items (data model, spikes, planner correctness, journal) come before leaf work like the report and CLI polish.

scores.evidence: "Security (M1): ... Path traversal through rendered names or a tampered journal ... Symlinks pointing outside the folder: skipped."
scores.rationale: Security has concrete treatment in M1 (and the tasks), but M2 and M3 have little explicit security content, such as supply-chain or release signing.

scores.evidence: "Observability (M1): The report shows a summary... --verbose logs each file... The journal serves as the audit trail."
scores.rationale: Observability is in M1 but is not threaded through M2 and M3 beyond a benchmark.

scores.evidence: "CI matrix of windows-latest, macos-latest, ubuntu-latest × Python 3.10/3.13... build wheel → install it in a clean venv"
scores.rationale: CI and a clean-venv wheel are reproducible, but there is no lockfile or pinned deps (exifread>=3), and the treatment is not threaded through all phases.

scores.evidence: "Reliability (M1): journal-before-rename, idempotent undo, group-level revert"; fault-injection test T10; M2 adds cycle temp-hop and sync warning.
scores.rationale: Failure handling is concrete from M1 (journal, undo, fault injection) and extends in M2 (cycles, sync folders) and in rollback.
The plan never mentions an AI layer or declares it N/A, although it adds no AI components, so it only partially addresses the question.

scores.evidence: Deferred table: "--recursive... Trigger: User has nested folders"; "Parallel metadata reads | Benchmark misses its target"
scores.rationale: Deferred items are explicit, each with a pull-forward trigger, and the non-goals are listed.

note: Strong, well-sequenced plan with a thin slice, decision gates and deferral triggers. Security, observability and reproducibility are front-loaded in M1 rather than threaded through every phase, and it never declares the AI layer N/A.
